source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Federal law requires parental consent for all STI testing and treatment of minors, so care cannot begin until a parent authorizes it.","B":"Minors can consent to STI services in every state and DC, but age, confidentiality, notification, and service-specific details can vary; apply current jurisdiction law and policy.","C":"Minors can consent to STI testing nationwide but never to treatment, so a parent must authorize medication in every jurisdiction.","D":"Only emancipated minors may independently consent to STI services; non-emancipated adolescents always require a parent to be present."}}
source_row.rationale: CDC states that every state and the District of Columbia explicitly allow minors to consent for their own STI services, while age provisions for some services and confidentiality or notification rules can vary. Therefore the nurse should recognize the general consent authority while applying current jurisdiction-specific law and policy and explaining confidentiality limits. The other options incorrectly impose universal parental-consent, testing-only, or emancipation requirements.
source_row.source_detail: CDC STI Treatment Guidelines — Adolescents, Legal Issues and Confidentiality: all 50 states and DC explicitly allow minors to consent for their own STI services; age provisions for some services and confidentiality/notification rules vary by jurisdiction. CDC STI Treatment Guidelines 2021 remain the live CDC guideline in 2026; page and legal caveats rechecked 2026-08-15. Current state law/policy must be applied at the point of care. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: prioritization, continuity, confidentiality, quality/cost-effective care, legal/ethical rights and assignment/delegation activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A 16-year-old seeks testing and treatment for a suspected sexually transmitted infection and asks whether parental consent is required. Which response is most accurate?
